UNDER THE HOOD
A price from the details.
Not from a hunch.
The interface helps you write a clear listing. Three trained models turn that text into an estimate.
01
Facts become a description
Make, model, year, mileage, condition and equipment are written as plain English. Your free-text notes are added in full. Nothing is secretly treated as a fixed price increase or deduction.
02
Words meet context
TF-IDF recognises informative words and phrases. A BERT-family MiniLM sentence encoder reads context in chunks of 254 wordpieces. The chunk embeddings are averaged and normalised.
03
Log price becomes dollars
Ridge regression combines the text signals to predict log(1 + price). We reverse that transformation to show a USD asking-price estimate. It does not guarantee a final transaction amount.
A longer story, without the 128-token cutoff
The complete model input can contain up to 8,000 characters. The notes field allows 6,500 characters, leaving room for your dropdown selections. Descriptions over 1,000 characters are split into as many 254-wordpiece chunks as needed. Every chunk is encoded; later details are not silently discarded at 128 tokens.
This is a lightweight BERT-family sentence model with pooled chunks, not a single 8,000-character attention window. TF-IDF reads the entire cleaned input as well.
What makes a useful description?
Useful
“2015 Corolla SE, 95,000 miles. One owner, clean title. Full service history, new brakes, small dent in the rear door.”
Less useful
“Amazing car! Bargain! Must go today!”
The model can only use facts you provide. Do not include your desired price, monthly payment, contact details or sales slogans. Common monetary expressions are redacted before prediction.
What this estimate can—and cannot—tell you
This model learned from US asking-price listings in April–May 2021. It has not been adjusted for inflation or today’s market. The reported test errors apply to original seller descriptions, not to a separately validated sample of people completing this form.
The 80% error band is derived from validation log-price residuals. It describes aggregate historical uncertainty, not a certified value, inspection result or guaranteed sale interval. Newer cars, rare models and cars outside the training price range need particular care.


MEASURED, NOT GUESSED
The numbers
behind the estimate.
A held-out comparison using the longer-description encoder deployed in this app.
Held-out results · log-price models
ModelMAERMSEMedian errorR²
MAE is average absolute dollar error. Median error is median absolute percentage error. Smaller is better for both. The combined model has similar dollar MAE to TF-IDF alone and a lower median percentage error on this test. More context does not automatically improve accuracy; one split does not establish statistical significance.
How the evaluation stays honest
Listings are sampled across the full source file, filtered to $1,000–$150,000, and deduplicated by exact cleaned text and valid VIN. The oldest 70% form training, the next 15% validation, and the newest 15% the held-out test set.
The TF-IDF vocabulary is fitted only on training text. Ridge regularisation is selected on validation dollar MAE. The BERT-family encoder is frozen. Test data is not used to choose the Ridge alpha or calibrate the error band. Near-duplicate dealer templates can still remain.
Source: Craigslist Used Cars Dataset · Public snapshot · Download evaluation JSON
